rules.statement: Add a new OAuth grant type as a registered extension-grant handler that advertises its grant_type, not by changing the token endpoint.
rules.why: The token endpoint already routes by grant_type to registered handlers (RFC 6749 section 4.5), so a new grant needs no endpoint change.
rules.check: Look for a new grant type implemented by adding grant_type branches to the token endpoint instead of registering a grant handler.

rules.statement: Leave powerful grants such as token exchange, client_credentials and password out of the default grant_types_supported, so an operator must opt in.
rules.why: A secure baseline supplies defaults, and a powerful grant must be enabled on purpose.
rules.check: Look for the token-exchange grant (or a similar powerful grant) added to the default supported grant types or turned on by default.

rules.statement: In token exchange, accept a subject_token or actor_token only when the authorization server's own issued-token validation accepts it; support an external issuer only by registering a separate validator, never in the core handler.
rules.why: Accepting tokens from external IdPs is a separate brokering capability, and it would widen every tenant's trust boundary by default.
rules.check: Look for token-exchange code that validates tokens against external or configured third-party issuers or keys inside the core grant handler or the default validator.

rules.statement: In token exchange, accept subject_token_type and actor_token_type values of access_token (under the access-token policy), id_token (under the ID-token policy) or jwt (only when it validates as one of those two), and reject any other type with invalid_request.
rules.why: Each token type must be validated under the policy for that type, and an unknown type must not be accepted.
rules.check: Look for an accepted token type outside these three, a jwt type accepted without validating as an access or ID token, or a rejection that uses an error code other than invalid_request.

rules.statement: Require the token-exchange requester to be a confidential client, and require each presented token to name it, either as client_id or in aud.
rules.why: Otherwise a client could exchange a token that was never meant for it.
rules.check: Look for a token-exchange path that allows public clients or skips the client_id/aud check on the subject or actor token.

rules.statement: For delegation token exchange, require the actor token to belong to the requester, the subject token's may_act.sub to equal the actor's sub (with client_id and iss matching when present), and the subject and actor to differ; the issued token carries an act claim that nests any act the subject token already holds.
rules.why: This is RFC 8693's act and may_act handling, so a resource server can audit and constrain what the actor does for the subject.
rules.check: Look for delegation code that skips the may_act comparison, allows subject == actor, leaves out act, or overwrites an existing act instead of nesting it.

rules.statement: Resolve a subject from validated token claims forward through the principal resolver, and never reverse a pairwise sub to recover the user.
rules.why: A pairwise sub must not be reversible, so a subject resolves only when forward resolution can find it.
rules.check: Look for code that maps a pairwise sub back to a user identifier, such as a reverse lookup or decrypting a pairwise value.

rules.statement: Compute token-exchange scopes as the requested, validated scopes, or else the subject token's scopes intersected with the client's allowed scopes, so an exchange never widens the requester's authority; resource and audience only narrow the issued audience.
rules.why: An exchange must never give the requester more authority than it already has.
rules.check: Look for exchanged tokens given the subject token's scopes without intersecting them with the client's allowed scopes, or an audience widened beyond what is requested and resolved.

rules.statement: In a token-exchange response, default requested_token_type to access_token, return a requested id_token in the access_token field with token_type N_A, and always include issued_token_type.
rules.why: RFC 8693 section 2.2.1 requires this response format.
rules.check: Look for a response without issued_token_type, an id_token returned in another field or with a token_type other than N_A, or a different default token type.

rules.statement: Issue a refresh token from token exchange only when the client's per-client setting allows it, and start its refresh-token family at the subject token's auth_time rather than at the time of the exchange.
rules.why: Refresh from an exchange is opt-in per client, and the family's fixed expiry horizon must not be extended by an exchange.
rules.check: Look for exchange code that issues a refresh token without checking the per-client allow setting, or that starts the family at the current time.

rules.statement: Reject token exchange of a token that is encrypted to a resource server's own key.
rules.why: The authorization server cannot validate a token encrypted to someone else's key, so it must not exchange it.
rules.check: Look for exchange paths that try to accept or pass through JWE tokens encrypted for a resource server.
